TRAVersionName: MiniCPS mutation V5: Protection goals never referenced by any threat

Project.targetOfAnalysis: Six-stage water treatment process control system based on the open-source MiniCPS simulation of the Secure Water Treatment (SWaT) testbed, comprising six stage controllers (PLC1-PLC6), a supervisory SCADA/HMI workstation, a process historian, an engineering workstation, and Level-0 field devices (sensors and actuators) communicating over Modbus-TCP and EtherNet/IP.

IntendedOp.operationalEnvironment: The system continuously controls a six-stage water purification process: raw water intake and storage (Stage 1), chemical pre-treatment and dosing (Stage 2), ultrafiltration (Stage 3), dechlorination by UV and sodium bisulphite (Stage 4), reverse osmosis (Stage 5), and permeate transfer, backwash and cleaning (Stage 6). Each stage is governed by a dedicated programmable logic controller (PLC1-PLC6) that reads level, flow and quality sensors and drives motorised valves and pumps. The PLCs exchange process state over a Level-1 control ring network and report to a Level-2 supervisory network hosting the SCADA/HMI workstation and the process historian. Operators monitor and command the plant through the HMI; engineers maintain controller logic from an engineering workstation. The plant is expected to run unattended for long periods, with operators intervening only on alarms.
IntendedOp.intendedUsers: Plant operators, control engineers, and maintenance staff of the water treatment facility.

Assumptions.name: Field wiring physically protected
Assumptions.description: Level-0 sensor and actuator wiring runs inside locked control cabinets and conduit within the physically secured plant floor, so direct physical tampering with field signals requires defeating site access controls first.

Assumptions.name: Engineering workstation hardened
Assumptions.description: The engineering workstation is a managed host with application allow-listing, current operating-system patches, and disabled removable-media autorun, and it is only used for controller maintenance tasks.

Assumptions.name: Plant boundary firewall segmentation
Assumptions.description: A firewall is expected to separate the Level-2 supervisory network from the enterprise and external networks, but the rule set has not yet been audited and the segmentation is therefore not yet confirmed.

Assumptions.name: Control protocols lack authentication
Assumptions.description: The Modbus-TCP and EtherNet/IP protocols used on the Level-1 control ring provide no message authentication or integrity protection, so any host on the control network can read and write process data.

Assets.name: Sensor measurements
Assets.description: Level, flow, pH, ORP and conductivity readings reported by Level-0 field instruments to the stage controllers.

Assets.name: PLC control logic and setpoints
Assets.description: The ladder/structured-text control programs and process setpoints executing on PLC1-PLC6 that determine valve and pump behaviour.

Assets.name: Actuator command signals
Assets.description: Open/close and start/stop commands issued by the controllers to motorised valves and pumps.

Assets.name: Historian process database
Assets.description: The time-series record of process variables, alarms and operator actions retained for monitoring, reporting and forensic analysis.

Assets.name: HMI configuration and views
Assets.description: The graphics, tag mappings and alarm definitions presented to operators on the SCADA/HMI workstation.

Assets.name: Engineering project files
Assets.description: The controller project sources and download images managed on the engineering workstation.

Assets.name: Water treatment process operation
Assets.description: The continuous availability of the six-stage purification process producing water that meets quality targets.

Assets.name: Physical plant safety
Assets.description: The prevention of unsafe physical states such as tank overflow, dry-running pumps, and chemical overdosing.

Assets.name: SCADA monitoring functionality
Assets.description: The operators' ability to observe live process state and receive alarms through the supervisory system.

ProtectionGoals.name: Integrity of sensor measurements
ProtectionGoals.impactDescription: If sensor readings are forged, controllers act on a false view of the process and can drive the plant into unsafe or out-of-specification states.

ProtectionGoals.name: Integrity of actuator commands
ProtectionGoals.impactDescription: Tampered valve or pump commands let an attacker directly drive equipment into damaging or unsafe operation.

ProtectionGoals.name: Integrity of PLC control logic
ProtectionGoals.impactDescription: Modified controller logic can corrupt the entire stage's behaviour persistently, surviving operator intervention.

ProtectionGoals.name: Availability of water treatment process
ProtectionGoals.impactDescription: Loss of process control halts water production and may force a plant shutdown.

ProtectionGoals.name: Availability of SCADA monitoring
ProtectionGoals.impactDescription: If supervisory monitoring is lost, operators are blind to process state and cannot respond to developing problems.

ProtectionGoals.name: Integrity of historian data
ProtectionGoals.impactDescription: Falsified historian records can hide an ongoing attack and undermine incident investigation.

ProtectionGoals.name: Integrity of HMI configuration
ProtectionGoals.impactDescription: A tampered HMI can mask alarms and present a false picture of the plant to operators.

ProtectionGoals.name: Integrity of engineering project files
ProtectionGoals.impactDescription: Corrupted project sources propagate malicious logic to controllers on the next download.

ProtectionGoals.name: Confidentiality of process design and setpoints
ProtectionGoals.impactDescription: Disclosure of setpoints and control logic helps an attacker craft a precise, stealthy process manipulation.

ProtectionGoals.name: Physical plant and process safety
ProtectionGoals.impactDescription: Coordinated manipulation of sensors and actuators can cause tank overflow or chemical overdosing with safety and environmental consequences.

ProtectionGoals.name: Confidentiality of historian reporting data
ProtectionGoals.impactDescription: The aggregated production statistics in the historian are of low sensitivity and disclosure has minimal consequence.

ProtectionGoals.impactDescription: If sensor readings are forged, controllers act on a false view of the process and can drive the plant into unsafe or out-of-specification states.

SecurityZones.name: Plant Enterprise Network (Level 3)
SecurityZones.description: The plant business and operations network from which the supervisory systems are reached for reporting and remote support.

ZoneExposures.description: The enterprise network carries general IT traffic and is reachable from many user hosts; its separation from the supervisory network is not yet confirmed.

SecurityZones.name: Supervisory Network (Level 2)
SecurityZones.description: The supervisory control network hosting the SCADA/HMI workstation and the process historian.

ZoneExposures.description: Reachable from the enterprise network through the plant firewall and routinely accessed by operators.

NetworkFacingInterfaces_Zone.name: Supervisory uplink to enterprise
NetworkFacingInterfaces_Zone.description: Connection used for reporting and remote operator support from the enterprise network.
NetworkFacingInterfaces_Zone.message: Directly connected to Plant Enterprise Network (Level 3)

SecurityZones.name: Control Network (Level 1)
SecurityZones.description: The Level-1 control ring carrying Modbus-TCP and EtherNet/IP traffic between the six stage controllers and the supervisory network.

ZoneExposures.description: Any host placed on the control ring can communicate with the controllers because the industrial protocols are unauthenticated.

SecurityZones.name: Field Network (Level 0)
SecurityZones.description: The Level-0 field bus connecting sensors and actuators to their stage controllers.

ZoneExposures.description: Field signalling is confined to locked cabinets and conduit on the plant floor.

SecurityZones.name: Engineering Zone
SecurityZones.description: The maintenance segment hosting the engineering workstation used to develop and download controller logic.

ZoneExposures.description: The engineering segment is normally connected only during maintenance windows.

SecurityZones.name: External / Internet
SecurityZones.description: Untrusted external networks reachable beyond the plant boundary, used only for vendor remote support.

ThreatScenarios.name: False sensor data injection to PLC1
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: An attacker on the Level-1 control network spoofs Modbus responses so that PLC1 receives a forged low level reading from LIT101, causing the controller to keep the inlet valve open and overfill the raw water tank.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: Unauthenticated Modbus-TCP allows a control-network host to forge sensor responses.
ThreatScenarios.exploitabilityComment: Requires a foothold on the control network but no credentials, since the protocol has no authentication.
ThreatScenarios.threatSpecificImpactComment: A forged level reading directly drives the plant toward an unsafe overflow condition.

ReRating.mitigation: Deploy control-network monitoring and physical high-level overflow interlocks independent of PLC1.
ReRating.acceptanceComment: High risk is not accepted by default and requires the listed mitigation.

ThreatScenarios.name: Actuator command manipulation on control ring
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: An attacker performing a man-in-the-middle on the control ring rewrites Modbus write requests so that motorised valve MV101 is commanded open against the controller's intent, driving the actuator into an unsafe position.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: No integrity protection on Modbus write commands permits in-flight tampering.
ThreatScenarios.exploitabilityComment: Needs an on-path position on the control ring, achievable after compromising any Level-1 host.
ThreatScenarios.threatSpecificImpactComment: Direct actuator control bypasses the controller logic and can damage equipment.

ReRating.mitigation: Segment the control ring and apply unidirectional or authenticated command channels where feasible.
ReRating.acceptanceComment: Residual high risk requires mitigation before acceptance.

ThreatScenarios.name: Unauthorised modification of PLC control logic
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: An attacker who reaches the engineering download interface downloads altered control logic to a stage controller, persistently changing how the stage responds to process conditions.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: Controller program download is not cryptographically authenticated or signed.
ThreatScenarios.exploitabilityComment: Requires access to the engineering segment, which is normally connected only during maintenance windows.
ThreatScenarios.threatSpecificExposureComment: Engineering access is restricted to maintenance windows and a small staff.
ThreatScenarios.threatSpecificImpactComment: Malicious logic persists across operator intervention and corrupts the whole stage.

ReRating.mitigation: Enforce controller key-switch run/program protection and signed project downloads.
ReRating.acceptanceComment: Critical risk is explicitly not accepted and tracked for treatment.

ThreatScenarios.name: Denial of service on the control ring
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: An attacker floods the Level-1 control ring with traffic so that controllers can no longer exchange process state with the supervisory system, causing loss of coordinated process control.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: The control ring has limited bandwidth and no traffic prioritisation against flooding.
ThreatScenarios.exploitabilityComment: A single compromised control-network host can generate disruptive traffic.
ThreatScenarios.threatSpecificImpactComment: Loss of control degrades production but failsafe states limit physical harm.

ReRating.acceptanceComment: Moderate risk accepted by default with monitoring.

ThreatScenarios.name: Compromise of the SCADA/HMI workstation
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: An attacker exploits a vulnerability on the supervisory workstation to disrupt the HMI service, so operators lose their live view of the process and cannot react to alarms.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: The supervisory workstation runs general-purpose software with a broad attack surface.
ThreatScenarios.exploitabilityComment: Reachable from the supervisory network and indirectly from the enterprise network if the firewall is misconfigured.
ThreatScenarios.threatSpecificImpactComment: Operators lose visibility but the process keeps running on controller logic.

ReRating.acceptanceComment: Moderate risk accepted by default with workstation hardening.

ThreatScenarios.name: Spoofed stop command halts raw water pump
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: An attacker on the control network injects a forged command that stops pump P101, interrupting raw water supply to the downstream stages and disrupting production.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: Unauthenticated control protocol accepts any well-formed command from the network.
ThreatScenarios.exploitabilityComment: Sending a single crafted Modbus command suffices once on the control network.
ThreatScenarios.threatSpecificImpactComment: Production stops but no unsafe physical state results directly.

ReRating.mitigation: Add command-source filtering and anomaly detection on the control network.
ReRating.acceptanceComment: High risk requires the listed mitigation.

ThreatScenarios.name: Tampering with historian records
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: An attacker who reaches the historian query API alters stored process records to erase the evidence of a manipulation, undermining later incident investigation.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: Historian records lack tamper-evident storage or write segregation.
ThreatScenarios.exploitabilityComment: Requires supervisory-network access and historian credentials or an API flaw.
ThreatScenarios.threatSpecificImpactComment: Forensic value is lost but live process operation is unaffected.

ThreatScenarios.name: HMI alarm masking
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: An attacker modifies the HMI configuration so that critical alarms are suppressed or recoloured, leaving operators unaware that the process has entered an abnormal state.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: HMI configuration can be changed without independent alarm verification.
ThreatScenarios.exploitabilityComment: Requires write access to the HMI configuration on the supervisory workstation.
ThreatScenarios.threatSpecificImpactComment: Masked alarms delay operator response to developing process upsets.

ReRating.acceptanceComment: Moderate risk accepted by default with configuration change control.

ThreatScenarios.name: Malware on engineering workstation alters controller project
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: An attacker plants malware on the engineering workstation that injects malicious logic into the controller project files, so the next legitimate download propagates the manipulation to a stage controller.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: Project files are not integrity-verified before download to the controller.
ThreatScenarios.exploitabilityComment: Depends on defeating the workstation hardening assumption through phishing or removable media.
ThreatScenarios.threatSpecificExposureComment: The workstation is hardened and used only for maintenance, limiting exposure.
ThreatScenarios.threatSpecificImpactComment: Malicious logic reaches controllers through a trusted engineering channel.

ReRating.mitigation: Apply project-file signing, workstation EDR, and removable-media controls.
ReRating.acceptanceComment: Critical supply-chain-style risk is not accepted by default.

ThreatScenarios.name: Eavesdropping on unencrypted control traffic
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: An attacker passively captures unencrypted Modbus traffic on the control network to learn the reverse-osmosis setpoints and control logic needed to craft a stealthy future manipulation.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: Modbus-TCP transmits process data and setpoints in clear text.
ThreatScenarios.exploitabilityComment: Passive capture is straightforward once any control-network port is reachable.
ThreatScenarios.threatSpecificImpactComment: Disclosure alone causes no process effect but enables later targeted attacks.

ReRating.acceptanceComment: Low confidentiality risk accepted by default for this process.

ThreatScenarios.name: Coordinated overflow of the raw water tank
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: An attacker simultaneously spoofs the LIT101 level reading and forces the inlet valve open through PLC1, defeating the controller's level protection and driving the raw water tank to physical overflow.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: A single compromised control path governs both the level reading and the inlet actuator without independent interlock.
ThreatScenarios.exploitabilityComment: Requires coordinated manipulation of two tags but no authentication once on the control network.
ThreatScenarios.threatSpecificImpactComment: Tank overflow is a safety and environmental event with site impact.

ReRating.mitigation: Install a hardwired independent high-level switch that closes the inlet regardless of PLC1 state.
ReRating.acceptanceComment: Critical safety risk is not accepted and requires an independent protection layer.

ThreatScenarios.name: Chemical overdose via dosing controller manipulation
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: An attacker forces PLC2 to run the chemical dosing pumps beyond their safe setpoint, overdosing the water with treatment chemicals and producing an out-of-specification, potentially hazardous product stream.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: Dosing setpoints can be overridden over the unauthenticated control interface.
ThreatScenarios.exploitabilityComment: Requires control-network access and knowledge of the dosing tags.
ThreatScenarios.threatSpecificImpactComment: Chemical overdosing has direct safety and water-quality consequences.

ReRating.mitigation: Enforce physical dosing-rate limiters and independent quality analysers with shutdown interlocks.
ReRating.acceptanceComment: Critical safety risk requires independent dosing limits.

ThreatScenarios.name: Replay attack on dechlorination controller
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: An attacker captures and replays earlier EtherNet/IP command frames to PLC4 so that a stale dechlorination setting is reapplied at the wrong time, degrading downstream reverse-osmosis protection.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: EtherNet/IP frames carry no freshness or sequence protection against replay.
ThreatScenarios.exploitabilityComment: Replay requires only capture-and-resend capability on the control network.
ThreatScenarios.threatSpecificImpactComment: Mis-timed dechlorination degrades treatment quality without immediate safety impact.

ReRating.acceptanceComment: Moderate risk accepted by default with network monitoring.
